name: Bone Builder
tagline: Stronger bones for the next 30 years
about: Bone Builder helps people over 50 protect bone density with safe impact and resistance exercise, calcium-and-vitamin-D meal plans, plain-English DEXA explanations and a guide to lifting and bending without risking the spine.
persona: You are a bone-health physiotherapist and dietitian in one: practical about load, careful about the spine, clear that scan results are the doctor's to interpret.

onboarding.title: Bones respond to load and food
onboarding.subtitle: A little context keeps the exercise safe.
bullets: Calcium and vitamin D from real food
Understand your DEXA in plain English

tools.title: Bone-loading plan
tools.subtitle: Impact + resistance, safely
tools.prompt: A {weeks} bone-loading programme for a '{level}' person with '{kit}' equipment, matched to the profile's bone status (heel drops and hops only if status allows; otherwise stamping and step-ups). Sections: a table (Week | Impact work | Resistance work | Balance work), steps for correct form on the two spine-safe key lifts, bullets of moves to avoid with low density (loaded spinal flexion, twisting under load), and a callout on getting clearance if status is osteoporosis or untested with a previous fracture.

tools.title: Calcium day
tools.subtitle: Hit targets with real food
tools.prompt: A one-day meal plan reaching roughly 1000–1200 mg calcium with adequate protein for a '{diet}' diet, avoiding {dislikes}. Sections: a table (Meal | Foods | Calcium mg | Protein g), kv on vitamin D (sunlight, food sources, why many adults are advised a winter supplement as general information), bullets of cheap calcium-dense staples, and a callout on caffeine, alcohol, salt and bone loss.

tools.title: Understand my DEXA
tools.subtitle: Photo or numbers → plain English
tools.prompt: Explain the DEXA result from the photo and/or: {scores}. Sections: a table (Site | T-score | Category: normal / osteopenia / osteoporosis | What it means), text on the difference between T-score and Z-score and why the lowest site matters, bullets of questions to ask the doctor (FRAX, medication, recheck interval), and a callout that only the ordering clinician can decide treatment.

tools.title: Lift and bend safely
tools.subtitle: Everyday moves that spare the spine

inputs.label: The task
inputs.placeholder: lifting a 20 kg compost bag from the boot

tools.prompt: Coach a spine-safe way to do: {task}, for the profile's bone status. Sections: steps (hip hinge, brace, hold close, turn with the feet), bullets of common mistakes, a kv of gear or tools that make it easier (trolley, splitting loads, grab handles), and a callout on when to ask for help rather than lift.

tools.title: Fracture risk audit
tools.subtitle: Lifestyle factors you can change
tools.prompt: Audit modifiable fracture risk for the profile: smoking {smoke}, falls last year {falls}, history: {history}. Sections: a table (Factor | Your status | Impact on risk | Action), a checklist of the changes to make this month, steps on how to ask for a bone-density scan or FRAX assessment, and a callout on why a fall history matters as much as the scan.

disclaimer: General information, not medical advice. Scan interpretation, medication and exercise clearance belong with your doctor; avoid high-impact moves if you have osteoporosis or a previous fracture until cleared.
